card.title: Safety Through Nonsense
card.instruction: Take control through elaborate impossible precautions, treating every objection as another reason the people present need protection.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Helmet on before reading the prophecy. We haven't inspected tomorrow for falling objects.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's one sentence. I just want to know if the picnic's on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Short prophecies concentrate the future. Read it through this oven glove.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It predicts sunshine. Surely that's safe.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Unfiltered future sunlight. Close the glove. Nobody reads another word until I've put sunscreen on tomorrow.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 mandates a helmet for tomorrow's falling objects, A3 adds an oven glove for concentrated prophecy, and A5 treats reassurance about sunshine as new exposure requiring a stop.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's short picnic question causes A3's concentrated-future warning; B4's sunshine finding causes A5's future-sunscreen intervention.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants a practical picnic answer and B4 supplies apparently reassuring content from the prophecy.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's safety evidence as another impossible risk, halting reading until A controls it.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes reading a prophecy and B2 the picnic decision it serves.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's sunscreen-on-tomorrow demand follows B4's actual sunshine content rather than a random precaution.
